guard: a startMembershipFeed startup that rejects drains every connection it had already opened
why: The leak is invisible to the feed itself: the function rejects with the caller's own error either
way, and a suite that tears down with `finally { feed?.stop() }` sees `feed` as undefined on a
reject, so the connection it should have closed is never named. The named cell therefore grades the
BROKER's connection table through CONNZ rather than anything the feed reports about itself.
The sibling cell asserting the rejection text cannot grade this alone: it passes both before and
after the fix, which is exactly why the leak survived.

mutations.name: the transactional drain closes nothing
mutations.expectRed: conn A is drained when startup rejects - no orphaned observer connection on the broker
mutations.cell: conn A is drained when startup rejects - no orphaned observer connection on the broker
mutations.note: Keeps the handler, the record and the rethrow, and drains an empty slice: the reported behavior with the tree still compiling and every other cell green. The connection count on the broker stays one above the baseline for the rest of the run.
